items.key_concept: ATP-citrate lyase inhibition upstream of HMG-CoA reductase
items.second_answer_attack: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition is the strongest competitor, but the stem explicitly identifies an upstream target and the label identifies ACL inhibition.

items.key_concept: soluble guanylate cyclase stimulation, increasing cGMP synthesis
items.second_answer_attack: PDE5 inhibition can also raise cGMP, but the vignette excludes reduced phosphodiesterase activity and the label identifies sGC stimulation.

items.key_concept: stabilization of the native transthyretin tetramer
items.second_answer_attack: RNA-level suppression could reduce precursor supply but cannot explain the stipulated direct effect in a cell-free TTR protein assay.

items.key_concept: nonabsorbed gastrointestinal potassium binding with increased fecal potassium excretion
items.second_answer_attack: Intracellular potassium shifting can reduce serum potassium but does not explain increased fecal elimination by a nonabsorbed polymer.
CFTR-mediated chloride secretion can affect luminal water, but the stipulated reduced apical sodium uptake and named drug uniquely identify NHE3.

items.key_concept: partial agonism of thyroid hormone receptor beta
items.second_answer_attack: THR-alpha activity is substantially weaker and does not match the beta-preferring receptor assay; the current label explicitly characterizes resmetirom as a THR-beta partial agonist.

items.key_concept: alpha4beta7 integrin blockade preventing interaction with MAdCAM-1 while alpha4beta1 function is not inhibited
items.second_answer_attack: Other immunologic targets may treat ulcerative colitis, but only alpha4beta7 explains the stipulated MAdCAM-1 adhesion result and preserved alpha4beta1 binding.

items.key_concept: antagonism of orexin receptors OX1R and OX2R
items.second_answer_attack: GABA-A positive modulation can promote sleep but is explicitly excluded by the stem and is not suvorexant's documented receptor mechanism.

items.key_concept: 5-HT2A inverse agonist and antagonist activity without appreciable dopamine D2 affinity
items.revision_interpretation: The current SPL version/effective date advanced in June 2026, while the full prescribing-information highlights explicitly display Revised: 4/2026. Under the candidate's declared revision_basis, 4/2026 is correct.
items.second_answer_attack: D2 antagonism is a familiar antipsychotic mechanism but is directly excluded by the documented lack of appreciable D2 affinity.

items.key_concept: reversible VMAT2 inhibition by major active circulating metabolites
items.second_answer_attack: The dopamine plasma-membrane transporter also moves monoamine but not from cytoplasm into synaptic vesicles; the stated subcellular transport step uniquely identifies VMAT2.
